P1.evidence: No setter, so nothing to read back. The usual compressed three-part frame — 'where are you today? Where do you want to be? If we can help, I can show you some options' — with what is in the way and what you need both absent. No agreement sought. Open question ran verbatim: 'I'll leave the floor to you, Christian. How can we potentially help you?'

P2.evidence: Two checks of nine. Age was asked; height and weight were not, on a call where the prospect's stated goals include getting leaner and keeping a six-pack. P2d is the best injury probe in this batch and deserves credit — 'you mentioned a few injuries like in your body. Are these more like aches and pains or is anything like chronic?' followed by 'And how are the shoulders now?' — which produced five surgeries and current symptoms. It then stopped dead: no dates, no surgeon or physio, no movement restrictions, no question about clearance. General health conditions and hereditary history were never asked. Training week, current results, diet, sleep and energy were all skipped entirely — for a competing bodybuilder and former personal trainer preparing for a HYROX race, not asking what he currently trains or eats leaves the entire programme design unsupported.

P3.evidence: The strongest laddering in the batch. The rep explicitly refused the scale-number framing up front — 'people typically get the best results with us, and I'll just, you know, chasing a number on the scale... they have a really clear picture as to what they want life to look like' — and the very first answer back was the real one: 'Honestly, just to be pain free.' He then drove the ripple hard and specifically: 'Are these just your clients or is there anyone else in your life that would benefit?', then 'I understand your clients, but your family and friends, how so?'. That reached the church, the men's fitness group and finally the vocational frame, where the follow-up 'By who?' produced 'The man above.' Getting from a six-pack to a sense of religious calling in eleven minutes is genuinely good work. Only the reflect-back is missing; the prospect in fact supplied his own, about overflow rather than pouring from an empty cup, and the rep acknowledged it rather than using it.

P4.evidence: One check of six. P4f ran and ran well — 'we live in the age of ChatGPT, YouTube, Instagram, there's so much information out there. So what's the rationale in terms of getting a coach as opposed to doing this yourself?' — and got a strong answer about wanting something structured and tailored from an actual human. Nothing else ran. The rep never asked what this prospect had tried, what happened with it, why it did not stick, or what is actually in the way, which is a striking omission given he is a former career personal trainer who has been following Trevor for up to a year without acting. The reason for that year of inaction was never established, and it turned out to be money.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame; the seventh consecutive call in this batch without one. P5d gets a partial for the want-or-need question, which was well followed up — 'It's a want, but it's what I see myself called to do' met with 'By who?' — and for the retrospective cost question at 00:20:25, 'if you had this before you entered your 30s, say at age 29, where do you feel like you could really be today?'. Both are good moves but both look backwards or sideways rather than forwards at the cost of inaction. The material was unusually strong and unused: five shoulder surgeries by 32, ongoing pain, a stated fear of waiting too long, and a HYROX race five months out.

P6.evidence: P6a ran cleanly at 00:20:54: 'do you feel internally capable of actually following the steps, working with Trevor, being a good student, and really applying yourself to this?' — 'Yep.' The alignment check also ran before the price and the rep pushed properly on the gap, 'why not a 12?', which produced the most self-aware answer of the call. But 8 out of 10 is not the clear yes the script requires, the all-in question was never asked, and — decisively — money was never isolated before the offer. The prospect had already flagged it himself at 00:18:22, 'I know I'm going to have some questions when it comes to prices. And is it at once? Is it biweekly? Is it monthly?', and that signal was not acted on until after two payment links had been sent and declined.

P11.evidence: The only call in this batch where a payment is witnessed completing on camera, but for the wrong product. P11a is partial: $200 was collected for Primal University, not a programme tier. P11b is not applicable — the Trevor onboarding call does not attach to Primal University and no programme was sold. P11c is a miss: no agreement email, no contract and nothing signed for a recurring subscription charge. P11d is partial and genuinely well done for what it was — the rep walked him through Skool account creation live, waited while he completed it and confirmed 'You're in, man.' Worth noting that this is the only instance in twelve files of the rep staying on the recording through a payment.

objection_plays.detail: The most complete run of the money play in this batch, alongside the Brandon Johnson call. Isolation was clean and correctly placed: 'money aside, you still want to do this. This is just about making it work for your finances, for your budget' — 'Yes.' Permission was sought. Then the full financial picture ran, every element: cash on hand ($300-400, 'and that's not including like gas or food'), number of credit cards (one), available credit ($3,000), credit score (mid-600s), monthly surplus after bills ($400), and investments ('Any other resources... like stocks, crypto?' — none). He even read the whole picture back for confirmation. By the playbook this is a hit. What it produced is the problem: the recommendation was 'we take a little bit of the credit card available amount', directed at the one credit line the prospect had explicitly said he was paying down to restore his limit, on $400 a month of disposable income. This is now the second call in three days where a completed financial picture was used to construct a payment from resources the prospect had just described as unavailable. The play has no stop condition and no threshold at which the correct output is to stop selling.

A clean timing objection with a specific, credible date attached: 'I want to say by the end of June, I should be set to get on', 'I have two more months before I get commission', and 'I'm going have to wait on that for a little bit, until I'm a little better financially.' None of the OD moves ran. No 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets'. And here, unusually, running the play would have been wrong anyway — the prospect's income genuinely does step change in two to three months, so the honest move was a firm diarised follow-up. That is broadly what happened, but it arrived after two payment links, a credit-card recommendation and a subscription sale rather than instead of them.

Hesitation surfaced at the alignment check — 'still waiting to see... sometimes I wait too long' — and the rep handled the visible part well by asking where he would be had he started three years ago. But the certainty question, the pleasure-versus-pain question, the PLANE and BRIDGE moves were all absent, and the prospect's own resolution ('if I waited till I was ready, I don't think I'll ever pull the trigger') was accepted rather than built on.
He never asked for thinking time; the deferral was purely financial and tied to a date.
No third-party approval gate raised at any point.

Clinical-fit gap, and on the raw facts the most serious presentation of it in this batch: five shoulder surgeries across both shoulders by age 32, symptoms ongoing, in a prospect whose primary stated goal is to be pain-free. The playbook contains no requirement to establish clearance, no question set for post-surgical history, and no path to defer a sale pending clinical sign-off. The rep asked two sensible opening questions and then had nowhere to go, so the shoulders became a selling point instead: 'alleviate any limitations of stiffness or aches and pains in your body, like the shoulders.' Kettlebell snatches, jerks and get-ups are overhead ballistic movements and are the single most relevant load class to a repeatedly reconstructed shoulder. Nothing in the process required anyone to notice that.

A gap worth adding to the known list: the prospect whose income step-change is imminent and dated. This is not affordability in the objection C sense and not timing in the objection D sense — it is a buyer who will be qualified in eight to twelve weeks and is not qualified today. There is no scripted play for parking a deal against a date, and the rep improvised one that is defensible in structure — a firm re-contact commitment — but reached it only after recommending credit-card drawdown and selling a subscription against $400 of monthly disposable income.

notes: Phase 3 here is the best in the batch and should be used as a coaching exemplar: the rep refused the surface goal, laddered through clients to family to church, and landed on a genuine vocational why in eleven minutes. Everything structural around it failed in the now-familiar pattern — two of nine baseline checks, one of six root-cause checks, no consequence frame, no money isolation before the offer. Two items are for the business rather than the rep. First, the instalment pricing: describing a 15-34% uplift as 'a slight bit of interest' is not a coaching issue. Second, the authority question — the rep justified continuing to sell to a man with $400 a month by citing the founder, 'Trevor says we shouldn't really let money get in the way', which is in direct tension with the sales manager's rule stated the previous day. Somebody needs to establish which of those is the policy.
